simple.meaning: דְּבוֹרָה (dᵉbôwrâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “the bee (from its systematic instincts).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דְּבוֹרָה (H1682) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Deuteronomy 1:44, with occurrences in Deuteronomy, Judges, Psalms, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דְּבוֹרָה (H1682) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דְּבוֹרָה (H1682) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דְּבוֹרָה (dᵉbôwrâh) / H1682 is traced through Deuteronomy 1:44, Judges 14:8, Psalms 118:12, Isaiah 7:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1682. deborah I. דְּבוֺרָה noun feminine bee (compare Arabic , swarm of bees , Aramaic דַּבַּרְתָּא , Syriac ) Isa 7:18 ; plural דְּבֹרִים Deut 1:44 ; Judg 14:8 ; Psa 118:12 . Read also דְּבֹרוֺ its bees 1Sam 14:26 for דְּבַשׁ ᵑ0 compare ᵐ5 We Dr.
definitions.rootNote: or (shortened) דְּבֹרָה ; from 1696 (in the sense of orderly motion);

occurrences.englishText: The Amorites, who lived in that hill country, came out against you and chased you as bees do, and beat you down in Seir, even to Hormah.
After a while he returned to take her, and he went over to see the carcass of the lion; and behold, there was a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.
It will happen in that day that Yahweh will whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
